description.narrative: Catalytic to present a conflict response model, as well as an integrated peacebuilding and area-based approach to address identified conflict drivers key conflict drivers and root causes of conflict in Tawilla, North Darfur

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).
UNDP as the Implementing Partner will comply with the policies, procedures and practices of the United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS.)

7 action plans developed 50% of the conflicts were for land and they were all solved 80 households received livelihoods support TBD at evaluation - % of targeted returnees and host community households stating an increase in household income. A total of 200 youth from Tawilla, Tebara, Khazan Tunjor, Dobo Alomda and Bobay sigili were trained in vocational skills (120 men trained in welding and 80 women trained in soap making) 7 sustainable and eco-friendly area-based plans designed 98 members (19% women; 27% youth) included in the plan development process One rural court established in Tarni village with 10 rural court judges (all men) Successfully completed the construction of one police post in Tawilla and deployment on going for operationalization and a supply of furniture items to enhance functionality. 35 police officers and ranks (all males) from Tawilla town, Tarni, Dobo Alomda and Terbara were trained in Tawilla locality One rural courts established and functioning, and 10 rural court judges (all men) and had their core capacities built on administration of justice and applying international standards on fair trial. 4 CBRMs were reactivated with a total number of 98 community members (19 women, 26 youth) 100% cases successfully mediated and resolved by CBRMs. 100% CBRMs stating increase in interactions and communication with other peacebuilding, rule of law and justice institutions at community, locality and state levels 100% community members stated increase in access to CBRMs for resolution of conflicts;

18: Number of awareness campaigns on women rights held 19; Number of women in associations accessing microfinance for improved empowerment disaggregated by age 20: Number of women centers/clubs established to enhance leadership skills and discuss women rights and regional treaties 21: Numbers of institutions whose capacities on human rights-based approaches and programming strengthened

800 community members (632 women inclusive of 320 youth) sensitized on women rights including international and regional treaties (CEDAW using drama and music and broadcast on local radio networks 200 women (inclusive of 87 young women) from Tawilla, Dobo Alomda, Tarni, Tabara and Tabit were trained in microfinance One woman center has been constructed in Tawilla, the center provides space for the women to do different activities such dialogues, peacebuilding meetings, microfinance savings and other livelihood initiatives. Strengthened the capacities of community-based organisations and CSOs and trained to apply a human rights-based approach in advocacy and programming that benefited a total of 35 participants out of which 18 were females drawn from five (5) CSOs led by women. While two (2) CSOs were led by youths.
